M_1_SQRTPI\n#define M_1_SQRTPI 0.564189583547756286948\n#endif\n\nenum OptionType {\n    CALL = 0,\n    PUT = 1\n};\n\nstruct OptionInput {\n    int type;           // CALL or PUT\n    double strike;      // Strike price\n    double spot;        // Spot price\n    double q;           // Dividend yield\n    double r;           // Risk-free rate\n    double t;           // Time to maturity\n    double vol;         // Volatility\n    double value;       // Expected value (for validation)\n    double tol;         // Tolerance\n};\n\n// Standard normal cumulative distribution function\ninline double cumulativeNormal(const double x) noexcept {\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + std::erf(x * M_SQRT1_2));\n}\n\n// Standard normal probability density function\ninline double normalPDF(const double x) noexcept {\n    return M_1_SQRTPI * M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\ndouble blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = option.spot;\n    const double K = option.strike;\n    const double r = option.r;\n    const double q = option.q;\n    const double T = option.t;\n    const double sigma = option.vol;\n    \n    if (T <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    \n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n   price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n    \n    return price;\n}\n\n// Standard test cases for validation\ninline constexpr std::array<OptionInput, 7> getTestOptions() noexcept {\n    return {{\n        {CALL, 40.00, 42.00, 0.04, 0.08, 0.75, 0.35, 5.0975, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0408, 1.0e-3},\n    }};\n}\n\n// Generate a larger set of options by scaling the test set\nvoid generateOptions(std::vector<OptionInput>& options, const size_t numOptions) {\n    constexpr auto testOptions = getTestOptions();\n    options.resize(numOptions);\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numOptions; ++i) {\n        // Cycle through test options and vary parameters slightly\n        const OptionInput& base = testOptions[i % testOptions.size()];\n        options[i] = base;\n        \n        // Add some variation for larger datasets\n        const double factor = 1.0 + 0.1 * (i / static_cast<double>(testOptions.size()));\n        options[i].spot *= factor;\n        options[i].strike *= factor;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResults(const std::vector<OptionInput>& options, \n                     const std::vector<double>& results) {\n    bool allPassed = true;\n    const int numChecks = std::min(static_cast<size_t>(10), expected=%.4f, rel_error=%.4e\\n\", \n               i, computed, expected, relError);\n        \n        // Relaxed validation - just check values are positive and reasonable\n        if (computed < false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return allPassed;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n    } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfzZtfWFti6xMeFSD9xgV","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The benchmark now prices options on the GPU with CUDA, and the executable is still `black_scholes`. The only files changed are `black-scholes/black_scholes.cpp` and `black-scholes/CMakeLists.txt`. The build is warning-free, and validation passes at every size I tried.\n\n**Performance** (RTX 3090, 1M options):\n\n| | Time | Options/s |\n|---|---|---|\n| Original (CPU) | ~90 ms | ~11M |\n| CUDA | ~6.3 ms | ~156M |\n\nThat is about 14× faster. The 10M run takes about 57 ms.\n\n**Design choices:**\n- **One thread per option.** The kernel scales with the number of SMs and the problem size.\n- **Options are generated on the device** from their index, using the same arithmetic as the original generator. Only the results cross PCIe, and the input array is no longer built on the host.\n- **Timed region** is the kernel plus the result copy-back. CUDA context setup and device allocation are excluded, so the number is comparable to the original, which timed only the pricing loop.\n- **Shared pricing code.** `blackScholes`, `makeOption`, and the CDF helpers are `__host__ __device__`, so the same formula runs on both sides.\n- **CMake:** the `.cpp` is compiled as CUDA via `LANGUAGE CUDA`, so no new files were needed. The minimum CMake version rose to 3.24 for `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native`, which targets whatever GPU is present. A CUDA toolkit is required; there is no CPU fallback.\n\n**Correctness caveat:** the output is not bit-identical to the original. Over 1M options the maximum relative difference is 2.8e-13 (mean 1.4e-14), and the `-r` hash changes from `6b004192aec33d5b` to `27ded655a431c265`. The cause is that CUDA's double-precision `erf`/`exp`/`log` differ from glibc in the last bits, and deep out-of-the-money prices amplify that through cancellation. Disabling FMA contraction did not restore the hash. If you need an exact hash match, the device math would have to be replaced with a glibc-matching implementation, or the prices computed on the CPU.\n\n**Not done:** the program uses only GPU 0. Splitting the work across the four GPUs on this machine would be the next step for multi-device scaling.\n\n`output.txt` shows a newer modification time than my starting copy, but I never wrote to it. I left it alone."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1044,"cache_read_input_tokens":45100,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1044},"output_tokens":6,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"98837219-43cd-4901-8358-7adc78d15357","uuid":"f8ae6468-6a5f-4716-8672-6a6b5c1f0807","timestamp":"2026-10-13T16:40:43.430Z","request_id":"req_011CfzZtfAfFVBTtSGoG9CnX"}
